## Welfare Experiment: Difference-in-Means

Loads the welfare survey experiment and estimates the wording effect by difference-in-means.

```{webr}
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)
# Read in data
data <- read.csv("data/welfare-small.csv")
n <- nrow(data)



# The DM estimator via OLS
model=lm(Y~D)
coeftest(model,vcov=vcovHC(model,type='HC2'))

# Directly computing the subsample mean difference.
Y=data$Y
D=data$D
tau_dm=mean(Y[D==1])-mean(Y[D==0])
tau_dm
```

## Regression-Adjusted Welfare Estimate

Reestimates the welfare wording effect after adding six observed covariates.

```{webr}
# Regress Y on D and W
model1=lm(Y~D+age+polviews+income+educ+marital+sex,data)
coeftest(model1,vcov=vcovHC(model1,type='HC2'))
```



## Monte Carlo: Difference-in-Means versus Regression Adjustment

Simulates 500 samples and compares the means and variances of DM and RA estimates.

```{webr}
set.seed(5280)
n <- 1000
B <- 500
tau_dm <- numeric(B)
tau_ra <- numeric(B)

for (b in seq_len(B)) {
  W <- rnorm(n, 2, 1)
  D <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)
  e <- rnorm(n)
  Y <- 1 + D + W^2 * D + exp(W) + e

  tau_dm[b] <- coef(lm(Y ~ D))["D"]
  Wc <- W - mean(W)
  tau_ra[b] <- coef(lm(Y ~ D * Wc))["D"]
}

c(mean_dm = mean(tau_dm), mean_ra = mean(tau_ra))
c(var_dm = var(tau_dm), var_ra = var(tau_ra))
```
